clue.text: Ian came round looking pale and sickly

indicators.note: coming round suggests the letters of the two words turn about into a new order

explanation.surface: Ian has come to looking washed out and unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came round' reads as recovering consciousness, but 'round' is the anagram signal on the letters of IAN CAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia, a shortage of red blood cells, leaves a person looking pallid and weak.

clue.text: Trees spring up round south

indicators.note: the turned word for spring wraps around the letter for south
in a down entry, going up means the word for spring is read bottom to top

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Trees shoot up around the southern side.
explanation.walkthrough: ASP is a poetic or dialect name for the aspen tree; SPA turned up gives APS, which goes round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Asp is an old and poetic word for the aspen, a kind of poplar tree.

clue.text: Size of field for a medley race

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters of race are mixed up

explanation.surface: How large a sports field must be to host a mixed relay race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley race' looks like swimming jargon, but 'medley' is the anagram signal on RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, traditionally used to measure fields.

clue.text: Harmony spray contains carbon by royal appointment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the carbon symbol inside them
a spray scatters things, so the letters of harmony are scattered

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A harmony-brand hair spray with carbon in it, made with a royal warrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harmony spray' suggests a product name; 'spray' rearranges HARMONY and C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is rule by a king or queen, so its offices are held by royal appointment.

clue.text: Length of pitch for batting after tea

indicators.note: the word for batting is placed after the word for tea

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
in cricket the side batting is said to be in

explanation.surface: A cricket groundsman measures the wicket before the batting resumes after tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket pitch is 22 yards long, which is exactly one chain, an old British unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: The chain, 22 yards, is the traditional measured length of a cricket pitch between the stumps.

clue.text: Remnant is substandard, needing price reduction

parts.note: food or a performance that is off is below par
a cut in prices is a reduction

explanation.surface: Leftover fabric is poor quality, so it has to be marked down.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is a leftover piece trimmed from a larger sheet of wood, cloth or paper.

clue.text: Draw attention to bearing in design fault

indicators.note: the bearing letter goes inside the rearranged letters
a design arranges things, so the letters of fault are rearranged

parts.note: N, for north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Pointing out a defect in an engineering design involving a bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like a machine part; it is a compass point, N, set inside FLAUT (from 'design' on FAULT).
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt something is to show it off conspicuously so others notice it.

clue.text: Don't miss what are said to be slogans

parts.note: to catch a ball or a train is not to miss it
words are what people say

explanation.surface: An advert urges you not to miss what are claimed to be great slogans.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchwords are popular phrases or mottoes adopted by a group, much like slogans.

clue.text: Divorcé in decisive court action?

definitions.meaning: a divorced man has broken the marriage tie, so humorously he breaks a tie
on a tennis court, the game that settles a set at six-all

explanation.surface: A divorced man takes part in a legal case that settles matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court action' suggests a lawsuit, but the court is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a tie-break decides a set level at six games each; a divorcé humorously breaks the knot.

clue.text: Fatherly friend swallows a tear

indicators.note: the word for friend takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: pal is a familiar word for a friend
a rent is a tear or rip in fabric

explanation.surface: A kindly friend gulps down a tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' suggests crying, but here it is a rip; 'swallows' makes the friend take A and the rip inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Parental means relating to a parent, so fatherly is a specific case of it.

clue.text: Keep a pupil in class

indicators.note: the letter for a pupil goes inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
L, for learner, stands for a pupil, as on learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A teacher detains a pupil in the classroom after lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb (keep in after school); it is the noun, a castle's fortified tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest central tower of a castle, so the word stands for the whole stronghold.

clue.text: Arrests sailor starting scraps

indicators.note: the word for sailor comes at the start, before the word for scraps

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
orts are scraps or leftovers of food

explanation.surface: Police arrest a sailor who is starting fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrests' suggests police; here it means halts, as a launch is stopped. 'scraps' looks like fights, but it is ORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To abort something is to halt it before completion, just as arresting a process stops it.

clue.text: Member of the first form at Westminster?

definitions.text: Member of the first form at Westminster?

parts.words: Member of the first form at Westminster?
parts.note: reads like a pupil at Westminster School, but the form is a bench and the Member an MP on the leading bench in the Commons

explanation.surface: A boy in the lowest class at Westminster, a famous London school.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is both a London public school and the seat of Parliament; the front benches seat ministers and shadow ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior MP who sits on the front bench in the House of Commons, as a minister or shadow minister.

clue.text: Clean one's teeth after sweet, sticky confection

indicators.note: the phrase for cleaning teeth is placed after the word for sweet

parts.note: candy is a sweet, especially in American usage
to floss is to clean between one's teeth with thread

explanation.surface: Brush your teeth after eating a sweet, sticky treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Candyfloss is spun sugar on a stick, a sticky fairground confection, also called cotton candy.

clue.text: Key worker not prepared to be dictated to

definitions.text: Key worker not prepared to be dictated to

parts.words: Key worker not prepared to be dictated to
parts.note: the worker presses keys and types from written drafts rather than from speech

explanation.surface: An essential employee refuses to be bossed about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' suggests an essential employee and 'dictated to' bullying; it is someone at a keyboard who types from written copy, not dictation.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a typist reproduces written documents on a keyboard, unlike a shorthand typist taking dictation.

clue.text: He dispensed with scruples some time ago

definitions.text: He dispensed with scruples some time ago

parts.words: He dispensed with scruples some time ago
parts.note: reads as a man who abandoned his morals, but he dispensed medicines measured in scruples, an old unit of weight

explanation.surface: Long ago a man cast his moral qualms aside.
explanation.walkthrough: A scruple was an apothecaries' weight of 20 grains; 'dispensed with' looks like 'abandoned' but means made up prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-time pharmacist who prepared and sold medicines, weighing drugs in scruples and drams.

clue.text: I am in pursuit in a carriage

indicators.note: the letter I goes inside the word for pursuit

parts.note: a chase is a pursuit

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are giving chase from a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise is a light, open, horse-drawn carriage for one or two people.

clue.text: A five-nil reverse that may be scrambled

indicators.note: a reverse result, read the other way, turns the run of letters back to front

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
nil means nothing, O

explanation.surface: A football team suffers a five-nil defeat that leaves them in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five-nil reverse' suggests a heavy defeat; 'reverse' turns A V O around. Ova are eggs, which may be scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova are eggs, and eggs are what get scrambled in the kitchen.

clue.text: Emancipated worker's carte blanche

parts.note: someone emancipated has been set free
a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: A freed labourer is given full licence to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a free hand means complete freedom to act as one sees fit, which is carte blanche.

clue.text: Dull, but not raining

definitions.meaning: a ... speech or book is dull and uninteresting

explanation.surface: The weather is grey but at least it is not wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull' looks like a description of an overcast sky, but it means boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry describes both tedious writing and weather without any rainfall.

clue.text: Game in which Tom goes nap

definitions.text: Game in which Tom goes nap

parts.words: Game in which Tom goes nap
parts.note: read as a tomcat settling down for a nap in its bed, and as nap, a card game term for bidding all

explanation.surface: A card game where a player called Tom bids to take every trick.
explanation.walkthrough: To go nap is to bid all five tricks in the card game nap; here a tom (male cat) naps in its bed, a cradle.
explanation.definitionFit: A string game played with loops passed between the fingers of two players, named for a cat's bed.

clue.text: Prompt delivery

parts.note: reads as a punctual parcel arrival, but means to bring on a baby's birth artificially

explanation.surface: A parcel arrives on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective meaning punctual; it is a verb, and the delivery is a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors bring on labour with drugs, prompting a birth before it starts naturally.

clue.text: Unidentified object could be a clay pigeon

definitions.meaning: a UFO, an unidentified flying object, popularly a disc-shaped alien craft
a clay pigeon is a disc that sails through the air like a dish

explanation.surface: Something unknown in the sky turns out to be a shooting target.
explanation.walkthrough: A clay pigeon is a clay disc flung into the air as a target for shooting practice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a supposed alien spacecraft and, literally, any airborne dish-shaped disc.

clue.text: States the time for practice

parts.note: the States, US, is the United States
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: America lays down the period allowed for training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practice' looks like training; it means customary use.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the habitual way something is done or a word is used.

clue.text: Wrestling with a problem, love?

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone asks their sweetheart if they are struggling with a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrestling with a problem' looks like struggling; 'Wrestling' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the traditional Japanese style of wrestling between heavy competitors.

clue.text: Reader's plea for original expression

parts.note: reads as a call for creative phrasing, but is a proofreader's mark asking that the original wording be kept

explanation.surface: A book lover begs writers for fresh turns of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: A reader here is a proofreader; the Latin mark means 'let it stand', cancelling a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin proofreading mark 'let it stand' restores the original wording after a deleted correction.

clue.text: It's unpleasant, but return to discharge debts

indicators.note: returning the word for discharge means reading it backwards

parts.note: to do a duty is to discharge it
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Being made to pay off what you owe is disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads the discharge word backwards; IOUs are written 'I owe you' notes acknowledging debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, a strong form of unpleasant.

clue.text: Stone pitcher

parts.note: reads as a jug made of stoneware, but is a device that hurls stones

explanation.surface: A stoneware jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitcher' looks like a jug; it is a thrower.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked stick with elastic, or a siege engine, used to fling stones.

clue.text: Get a seat when prepared to stand

parts.note: set means ready or prepared
a tee is the peg a golf ball stands on

explanation.surface: Find a chair once you are ready to get up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' looks opposed to sitting; it is a golfer's tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is an upholstered seat for two or more people, a sofa.

clue.text: Last to finish with majority

parts.note: the end is the finish
most means the majority

explanation.surface: A runner coming in last to finish with most of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means furthest towards the end, the final one in a row.
